Elena: FYI — canary shows a p99 latency spike when prefix/cache hit fraction is ~65-80%. p50 steady (~110ms) but p99 jumped 120ms -> ~240ms after the recent batching change. :eyes:
Sam: ugh. kernel selection or batching windows? can you paste profiler snippets and the batch meta?
Elena: here's a trimmed profiler dump from the canary (model: redwood/gpt-medium-quant). note the alternating kernel choices around high cache-hit bursts:
```
[2026-03-10 11:22:03] batch_id=1245 tokens=512 effective_len=24 cache_hit_frac=0.72
kernel_choice: fused_attn_fp16 (expected)
kernel_time_ms: 36.4
queue_wait_ms: 8.2
-- next microbatch --
[2026-03-10 11:22:03] batch_id=1246 tokens=512 effective_len=6 cache_hit_frac=0.95
kernel_choice: matmul_fp16
kernel_time_ms: 89.1   <-- big jump
queue_wait_ms: 7.9
selector_confidence: low (seq_len var high)
```
Elena: you can see short effective lengths (due to prefix hits) but the selector flips to `matmul_fp16` which is slower for these mixed batches because we end up with high kernel-launch overhead + less efficient fused path when some sequences are long and others are short.
Aisha: yep — this is the classic "cache-hit induced heterogeneity" problem. When many requests are prefix hits, the avg sequence length distribution becomes bimodal: lots of tiny remaining tokens + few full-length new prompts. Our kernel selector currently uses mean seq_len per-window and picks kernels per-batch, so it oscillates.
Aisha: proposal: dynamic windowing with a hit-aware token budget. Instead of a fixed token budget of N tokens per forming batch, use a sliding window that computes two stats: median_remaining_tokens and cache_hit_fraction. If hit_frac > 0.6 and median_remaining_tokens < threshold, prefer fused_attn path and tighten the max_batch_len to reduce matmul migrations. Example config snippet:
```
batching:
  token_budget_target: 1024
  dynamic_windowing: enabled
  hit_aware_threshold: 0.6
  median_len_threshold: 16
  family_preference: {
    fused: 0.8,
    matmul: 0.2
  }
```
Aisha: this biases kernel selection and admission so we avoid switching to the heavier matmul kernel when the workload is dominated by tiny remaining token runs.
Jordan: we ran a short canary (30m) with that config on canary-3. Results: p99 dropped from 240ms -> 165ms (improvement ~75ms), p50 unchanged, throughput steady (+-2%). Kernel-mismatch events reduced from 18% -> 4%.
Jordan: sample metric dumps:
```
canary: dynamic-windowing=true
p50_latency_ms: 112
p99_latency_ms: 165
kernel_mismatch_rate: 0.04
avg_batch_size_tokens: 876
```
Sam: nice. any regression on cold (no-cache-hit) traffic?
Jordan: tested 10% cold traffic spike, p99 for cold-only stayed within 10% of baseline. We did see slightly lower ideal packing efficiency for pure cold because of the conservative bias, but overall token/sec was ~-1.5%.
Sam: sounds acceptable. couple of asks: (1) add queue_time_ms telemetry to vet admission/backpressure (we saw queue_wait_ms ~8ms in trace), (2) please add a control flag so we can A/B revert quickly.
Elena: added both to the rollout plan. command used to start the canary: `./deploy_canary --cfg batching.dynamic_windowing=true --duration 30m --trace-level kernel,queue`
